- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope in that window.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment; weight recent 7-day sentiment more heavily than 18-day average.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common; apply “cool-down” rule: if sentiment >0.80 for 3+ days, cap forecast at 10% below recent peak.
